title: GeoBrowse: A Geolocation Benchmark for Agentic Tool Use with Expert-Annotated Reasoning Traces
headline_result: GATE (the paper's own agentic workflow) outperforms direct inference and open-source agents; no single quantitative headline score or human-performance gap is given for a specific model.
search_tools_named: GATE toolkit: 5 think-with-image tools (crop, rotate, pixel analysis, auxiliary lines, super-resolution) + 4 knowledge tools (web text search, web image search, visit, code interpreter)
task_summary: Given an image with weak or obfuscated clues, identify the depicted location by inspecting the image closely and searching the web for corroborating evidence.
task_phrase: GeoBrowse is a geolocation benchmark designed to evaluate three agentic capabilities: visual cue composition , open-web information seeking and verification , and tool-use planning

title: GeoDisaster: Benchmarking Orchestrated Agents for Operational Disaster Geo-Intelligence
headline_result: Not a single number; qualitative finding is that GeoDisaster 'challenges existing RS-VLMs and agentic systems, while RCEA improves tool use, evidence grounding, state consistency, and decision generation'; no specific model/score named.
search_tools_named: 18 disaster-oriented geospatial tools covering evidence access, spatial analysis, damage assessment, exposure estimation, and structured reporting, operating over optical/SAR imagery, raster masks, vector geometries, road networks, and exposure layers
task_summary: Given a disaster scenario with satellite imagery and GIS data, use geospatial tools to assess damage, estimate exposure, and generate a structured report.
task_phrase: Instances integrate heterogeneous EO/GIS evidence—optical and SAR imagery, raster masks, vector geometries, road networks, and exposure layers—spanning hazard detection, damage assessment, exposure estimation, and diagnostic report generation.

title: GraphWalk: Enabling Reasoning in Large Language Models through Tool-Based Graph Navigation
headline_result: tool-based traversal yields substantial and consistent gains over in-context baselines across all model families tested, with gains becoming more pronounced as scale increases, precisely where in-context approaches fail catastrophically
search_tools_named: graph navigation tools (find node by property, get neighbors, get distinct property values, maze-style get_next_possible_cells/get_path) each equivalent to a Cypher query on the graph database, plus a non-query 'think' logging tool
task_summary: Given a multi-hop question over a large knowledge graph, navigate it step by step with graph query tools to compute the answer.
task_phrase: GraphWalk equips the LLM with a minimal set of orthogonal graph operations just enough to traverse any graph structure

title: Evaluating Deep-Search Agents under Hierarchical Web Evidence Poisoning
search_tools_named: a Search(q') action (returns result metadata: title/url/timestamp, no page body) and a Scrape(u) action (returns full page content), operating over a controlled corpus of clean and injected poisoned web pages; compared against a Static Full-Context single-Search-call baseline
task_summary: Given a consumer question, search and scrape a web corpus seeded with persuasive misinformation, then recommend an answer while verifying and recovering from bad evidence.
task_phrase: HAE-GEO , a benchmark that tracks the full trajectory from exposure to recovery under progressively more persuasive Web poisoning.

title: HETERQA: Benchmarking Record Retrieval over Multiple Heterogeneous Sources
headline_result: Hybrid retrieval achieves the strongest Recall@10 and Self-RAG achieves the best MRR@10, but all evaluated methods remain far from saturating the benchmark; no human baseline is stated.
search_tools_named: sparse (BM25), dense (DPR, ANCE, KALM, Llama, Qwen3, Qwen3-VL), late-interaction (ColBERT, ColPali), hybrid (BM25+dense RRF fusion), and agentic retrievers over relational tables, text, images, spatial data, and knowledge graphs
task_summary: Given a query with constraints spanning multiple data types, retrieve the exact records satisfying all constraints across tables, text, images, maps and graphs.
task_phrase: Each question require methods to retrieve records that jointly satisfy all source-specific constraints.

title: HMARS: A Hierarchical Multi-Agent Memory System for Long-Context Reasoning
headline_result: HMARS achieves the best overall performance against retrieval, reranking, full-context, graph-based, and agentic long-context baselines across long-document and multi-turn memory tasks; no single numeric figure given in the abstract.
search_tools_named: hierarchical multi-agent memory access: sub-agents perform query-conditioned assessment over bounded local memory regions of the given long document/interaction history, mid-agents coordinate regional context, and a frontier model reasons over the retrieved evidence pages (contrasted with a Dense Rerank baseline built on a standard dense retriever + Qwen3-8B reranker)
task_summary: Given a very long document or multi-turn interaction history, find and integrate evidence scattered across it to answer a question.
task_phrase: Long-context reasoning requires models to access, retrieve, and integrate evidence scattered across documents, dialogues, and accumulated interaction histories.

title: SenseNova-MARS: Empowering Multimodal Agentic Reasoning and Search via Reinforcement Learning
headline_result: SenseNova-MARS-32B scores 74.3 on MMSearch and 54.4 on HR-MMSearch, surpassing proprietary models such as Gemini-3-Pro and GPT-5.2.
search_tools_named: text search (Serper Search API, top-5 results summarized by Qwen3-32B), image search (Serper Image Search API, reverse image search), and image crop (local zoom/crop tool for fine-grained perception); training-time text retrieval uses a local Wikipedia KB and Playwright+BeautifulSoup HTML fetch, while inference uses live Serper search
task_summary: Given a high-resolution image and question, zoom into image regions and search the web for text or visual matches to answer accurately.
task_phrase: SenseNova-MARS tackles the challenging visual task by leveraging an integrated suite of text search, image search, and image crop tools within the reasoning process.

title: HalluHard: A Hard Multi-Turn Hallucination Benchmark
headline_result: Hallucinations remain substantial even with web search: approximately 30% for the strongest configuration, Opus-4.5 with web search.
search_tools_named: provider-native web-search variants for GPT and Claude families (API default settings); Gemini web search via Vertex AI Search (excluded from evaluation because its links could not be opened by the judge); open-weight models evaluated without search (unsupported natively)
task_summary: Given a multi-turn conversation about niche or fabricated facts, answer with cited claims that are actually supported by the cited sources.
task_phrase: During generation, models are instructed to support factual claims with explicit citations, providing a concrete anchor for verification.

title: HawkBench: Investigating Resilience of RAG Methods on Stratified Information-Seeking Tasks
search_tools_named: BGE-M3 dense retriever as the main baseline retriever (top-k=5); ablations additionally compare sparse retrieval and a dense+sparse hybrid; retrieval is over a fixed, curated multi-domain corpus of 229 long documents (textbooks, financial reports, legal contracts, novels, academic papers)
task_summary: Given a factoid or open-ended rationale question, retrieve from a domain-specific document corpus and produce an accurate, well-supported answer.
task_phrase: HawkBench offers: (1) systematic task stratification to cover a broad range of query types, including both factoid and rationale queries, (2) integration of multi-domain corpora across all task types to mitigate corpus bias, and (3) rigorous annotation for high-quality evaluation.

title: Haystack Engineering: Context Engineering for Heterogeneous and Agentic Long-Context Evaluation
headline_result: even advanced models like Gemini 2.5 Pro and GPT-5 suffer cascading failures from self-generated distractors or struggle to perform early stops; no single numeric headline accuracy is given in the abstract.
search_tools_named: BM25 (sparse), Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B (dense), BM25+dense hybrid via reciprocal rank fusion, Personalized PageRank (PPR) graph-based reranking, over the full English Wikipedia hyperlink network
task_summary: Given a multi-hop question buried in a long, retriever-built noisy context, find the answer, refining queries across rounds and deciding when to stop.
task_phrase: HaystackCraft further extends NIAH to dynamic, LLM-dependent settings that simulate agentic operations, where models refine queries, reflect on their past reasonings, and decide when to stop.

title: HiEviDR-Bench: A Benchmark for Hierarchical Evidence Aggregation in Deep Research
headline_result: 16 representative multimodal LLMs show performance drops markedly on citation accuracy, claim construction, and answer correctness despite strong report quality (no single named model/number given).
search_tools_named: Qwen3-VL-Embedding-2B dense retriever over a fixed multimodal (text+image) corpus built from Wikipedia and arXiv papers
task_summary: Given a question and a fixed multimodal document collection, gather text and image evidence across sources and write a grounded evidence-aggregation report.
task_phrase: In the RAG setting, the model receives the user query together with a fixed set of retrieved multimodal evidence, and then directly generates the final report in a single pass.

title: On Path to Multimodal Historical Reasoning: HistBench and HistAgent
headline_result: HistAgent (built on GPT-4o) achieves 27.54% pass@1 / 36.47% pass@2, vs. GPT-4o alone 18.60%, DeepSeek-R1 14.49%, and Open Deep Research-smolagents 20.29% pass@1 / 25.12% pass@2 -- no explicit human baseline given.
search_tools_named: OCR (Transkribus, Asian-script OCR), multilingual translation, reverse image search, Google Books/Google Scholar/Springer Nature API literature search, PDF/DOCX/XLSX/PPTX file tools, image analysis tool
task_summary: Given a historical question over multilingual, multimodal primary sources, interpret manuscripts or images and produce an accurate, well-cited answer.
task_phrase: The tasks span a wide range of historical problems—from factual retrieval based on primary sources to interpretive analysis of manuscripts and images, to interdisciplinary challenges involving archaeology, linguistics, or cultural history.

title: HopRefusalBench: Diagnosing Refusal Failures in Search-Augmented Agents for Multi-Hop Reasoning
headline_result: Across ten frontier proprietary and open-weight models in search-augmented mode, the best model achieves a target-aware correct halting rate (TCHR) of only 42.9% (no specific model named in abstract).
search_tools_named: a local retriever over a 2018 Wikipedia snapshot using E5 dense embeddings, invoked through the model's native tool-calling interface, up to 8 search calls returning top-3 documents each
task_summary: Given a question that may be unanswerable or based on a false premise, search step by step and either answer or appropriately refuse.
task_phrase: Reliable search-augmented agents should detect unanswerable or ill-posed queries during multi-step retrieval and respond with an epistemically appropriate non-answer.

title: HotelQuEST: Balancing Quality and Efficiency in Agentic Search
venue: Conference of the European Chapter of the Association for Computational Linguistics
headline_result: LLM-based agents achieve higher accuracy than traditional retrievers but at substantially higher cost due to redundant tool calls and suboptimal routing (no single specific system named).
search_tools_named: three specialized tools: retrieving hotel Descriptions and retrieving customer Reviews (both dense retrieval over Milvus indices, FLAT for descriptions and HNSW for reviews, All-MiniLM-L6-v2 embeddings), and Web Search via the Tavily API; compared against pure retrieval baselines (BM25, dense retrievers with Qwen3-Reranker)
task_summary: Given a hotel search query with possibly vague preferences, retrieve hotel data, reviews, or web results to answer accurately and cheaply.
task_phrase: a benchmark comprising 214 hotel search queries that range from simple factual requests to complex queries, enabling evaluation across the full spectrum of query difficulty.

title: Benchmarking Hybrid Deep Research Across Database Querying and Web Search
headline_result: Even state-of-the-art models (GLM-5.2, Claude-Sonnet-4.6, GPT-5) achieve only about 50-54% Pass@8 on the hard subset.
search_tools_named: SQL query execution over LiveSQLBench-Base-Lite databases, and web search over public evidence drawn from Wikipedia and FineWeb-10BT
task_summary: Given a mixed structured/unstructured question, query a database and search the web, passing constraints between them to reach one verified answer.
task_phrase: Every task is strictly tool-dependent, requiring successful execution of both SQL queries and web searches.

title: From Inertia to Objectivity: Improving Deep Research Agents with Noise Isolation
search_tools_named: SearchAgent toolkit (Table 8): web_search (Google), fetch_html, fetch_pdf, visit_page (downloads page or returns YouTube transcript), find_archived_url (web archive lookup), inspect_file_as_text
task_summary: Given a complex question, iteratively search and browse web pages, deciding when to keep searching versus visit a page, until confident enough to answer.
task_phrase: repeating this loop until enough evidence is collected to report back to the manager

title: ICBCBench: An Industry Consortium Benchmark for Financial Deep Research
search_tools_named: Search API, Web Browser, Multi-modality (OCR/multimodal), Coding, File tools; e.g. Serper for search and Jina for web crawling in the MiroThinker deployment
task_summary: Given a financial research query, retrieve and reason over multiple sources to answer verifiable questions or write an analyst-style report.
task_phrase: Given a user query, a DRA can execute a full research pipeline, including problem analysis, research planning, iterative retrieval and reasoning, and the integration of information from diverse sources, ultimately producing a structured report comparable to that of professional research analysts.

title: One Interaction Is Worth a Thousand Guesses: Benchmarking the Interactive Capabilities of Deep Research Agents
search_tools_named: Tavily API for information retrieval, within an Open Deep Research (LangChain-AI) agentic framework with Planner/Supervisor/Researcher/Reporter/Evaluator/Questioner roles
task_summary: Given an underspecified research request, decide whether to ask a simulated user clarifying questions while researching, then write an aligned report.
task_phrase: IDRBench formulates deep research as an interactive process where agents may solicit clarification to better align with user intent.

title: HyperEyes: Dual-Grained Efficiency-Aware Reinforcement Learning for Parallel Multimodal Search Agents
headline_result: HyperEyes-30B surpasses the strongest comparable open-source agent by 9.9% in accuracy with 5.3x fewer tool-call rounds on average, across six benchmarks.
search_tools_named: image_search (visual grounding fused with image retrieval for a grounded region, as a single atomic action) and text_search (textual query retrieval)
task_summary: Given an image with multiple entities and a question, search for all entities concurrently rather than one-by-one, then answer.
task_phrase: The Image Multi-Entity Benchmark (IMEB) addresses this gap by elevating search efficiency to a primary evaluation axis, constructing queries that require concurrent localization and retrieval across multiple entities.

title: InfoDeepSeek: Benchmarking Agentic Information Seeking for Retrieval-Augmented Generation
headline_result: not stated in abstract (no single headline agent-performance number given)
search_tools_named: Google, Bing, Yahoo, DuckDuckGo search engines; Selenium-based browser tool; auxiliary time-calculation tool
task_summary: Given a tricky factual question, search and browse the live web to find, verify, and compactly summarize accurate supporting evidence.
task_phrase: a new benchmark with challenging questions designed for assessing agentic information seeking in real-world, dynamic web environments

title: InfoMosaic-Bench: Evaluating Multi-Source Information Seeking in Tool-Augmented Agents
headline_result: GPT-5 achieves the best reported result among 14 evaluated LLM agents, with only 38.2% accuracy and 67.5% pass rate.
search_tools_named: a web-search tool plus 77 MCP tools across 7 servers spanning medicine/biology, finance, maps, and video domains; ReAct framework with OpenAI's tool-calling interface and a Python Sandbox for executing tool calls
task_summary: Given a multi-domain question, combine web search with specialized medical, finance, maps, or video tools to derive one verified answer.
task_phrase: InfoMosaic-Bench requires agents to combine general-purpose search with domain-specific tools

title: InterLV-Search: Benchmarking Interleaved Multimodal Agentic Search
headline_result: best model below 50% overall accuracy; no specific model is named in the abstract.
search_tools_named: InterLV-Agent tool suite: image search, reverse image search, web search, webpage browsing, image cropping, code execution; offline multimodal retriever for Level 1/2 over the benchmark corpus
task_summary: Given a query with visual clues, alternate between searching, browsing, and inspecting images so each new piece of evidence guides the next search.
task_phrase: in which textual and visual evidence is repeatedly used to condition later search

title: InteractComp: Evaluating Search Agents With Ambiguous Queries
headline_result: Best of 17 evaluated models achieves only 13.73% accuracy on ambiguous queries despite reaching 71.50% accuracy when given complete context.
search_tools_named: Google Serper API (google.serper.dev/search), top-5 organic results per query; a non-search 'ask' action for posing closed-ended clarifying questions to a simulated user
task_summary: Given an ambiguous question, search the web and ask clarifying yes/no questions to resolve ambiguity before giving a verifiable answer.
task_phrase: InteractComp evaluates whether agents can recognize ambiguity and actively gather necessary context through interaction during the search process

title: IoDResearch: Deep Research on Private Heterogeneous Data via the Internet of Data
venue: IEEE International Conference on Acoustics, Speech, and Signal Processing
search_tools_named: IoD search tools via Model Context Protocol (MCP): digital-object retrieval, content-chunk retrieval, and knowledge-graph fine-grained (atomic-fact/subgraph) retrieval, using keyword search, vector similarity, KG-based reasoning, and hybrid recall strategies; plus a code tool for data analysis, visualization, and chart generation
task_summary: Given a question over private, heterogeneous scientific data, retrieve multi-granularity evidence and either answer it or write a structured report.
task_phrase: a multi-agent system supports both reliable question answering and structured scientific report generation

title: K-BrowseComp: A Web Browsing Agent Benchmark Grounded in Korean Contexts
headline_result: Frontier LLMs (GPT-5.5, DeepSeek-V4-Pro, GLM-5.1) reach only 30.00-45.67% on the Verified subset; Korean domestic models only 0.00-10.33%; strongest model reaches 26.00% on the adversarial synthetic split.
search_tools_named: Perplexity Search API
task_summary: Given a hard question requiring Korean-language web sources, search the web to find one short, verifiable answer.
task_phrase: a web-browsing agent benchmark grounded in Korean contexts, consisting of 400 problems

title: KARL: Knowledge Agents via Reinforcement Learning
headline_result: KARL is Pareto-optimal on KARLBench across cost-quality and latency-quality trade-offs compared to Claude 4.6 and GPT 5.2, including out-of-distribution tasks; no single accuracy percentage given.
search_tools_named: a single Vector Search tool over a fixed closed corpus per task (embedding model varies: Qwen3-8B for BrowseComp-Plus, GTE-large for PMBench, Qwen3-0.6B for TREC-Biogen/QAMPARI/FinanceBench/FreshStack)
task_summary: Given an enterprise-style query, iteratively search a fixed document corpus to gather and synthesize evidence into one grounded answer.
task_phrase: KARLBench, a multi-capability evaluation suite spanning six distinct search regimes, including constraint-driven entity search, cross-document report synthesis, tabular numerical reasoning, exhaustive entity retrieval, procedural reasoning over technical documentation, and fact aggregation over internal enterprise notes

title: Towards Knowledgeable Deep Research: Framework and Benchmark
venue: Annual International ACM SIGIR Conference on Research and Development in Information Retrieval
headline_result: HKA outperforms most existing DR agents on general-purpose and knowledge-centric metrics and surpasses the Gemini DR agent on vision-enhanced metrics (specific numeric scores not given in the abstract).
search_tools_named: Planner dispatches to an Unstructured Knowledge Analyzer (Serper as web search API, Crawl4AI as web crawler/browser tool) and a Structured Knowledge Analyzer (dense retrieve-and-rerank over tables via text-embedding-3-small/FAISS, then a code LLM (Qwen3-Coder) executing code to build figures/tables, then a vision-language model (Qwen3-VL) to derive insights)

title: Diagnosing and Addressing Pitfalls in KG-RAG Datasets: Toward More Reliable Benchmarking

task_summary: Given a natural-language question, retrieve and reason over a knowledge graph to produce a correct, verifiable multi-hop answer.
task_phrase: Knowledge Graph Question Answering (KGQA) systems rely on high-quality benchmarks to evaluate complex multi-hop reasoning.

title: Ko-WideSearch: A Korean Breadth-Search Benchmark for Exhaustive Set Enumeration by Web Agents
headline_result: Across twenty web agents, Item-F1 reaches 92.8 but Row-F1 only 53.7, showing agents recover the set but not the full per-row attribute tables (no single best model individually named).

task_summary: Given a Korean category like a TV season or dynasty, search out every member of that set and fill in an attribute table for each one.
task_phrase:
Each task names a set-parent entity—a TV season, a dynasty, a league, an administrative
region, an election—and asks for its full membership plus a per-item attribute table

title: Detecting Knowledge Inconsistencies Across Text, Tables, and Knowledge Graphs
search_tools_named: Text-to-SPARQL query generation (via GRASP) executed against a fixed 2025-05-10 Wikidata snapshot through the QLever SPARQL endpoint
task_summary: Given a table-QA question, query a knowledge graph for the same answer and detect and explain any inconsistency with the table's answer.
task_phrase: This raises a practical question: when these modalities disagree, how can we detect and explain the conflict?

title: KramaBench: A Benchmark for AI Systems on Data-to-Insight Pipelines over Data Lakes
headline_result: The best system reaches only 55% end-to-end accuracy in the full data-lake setting (62% with perfect retrieval); leading LLMs identify up to 42% of important data tasks but fully implement only 20% of individual data tasks; no specific model is named as the best system.

task_summary: Given a messy multi-file data lake and a question, design and run a data-processing pipeline to produce a correct analytical answer.
task_phrase: KramaBench evaluates the capabilities of systems to generate data science pipelines over a data lake consisting of heterogeneous, unclean input.

title: LABBench2: An Improved Benchmark for AI Systems Performing Biology Research
headline_result: Frontier models show substantially improved ability on both LAB-Bench and LABBench2 over time, but LABBench2 is meaningfully harder, with model-specific accuracy dropping by -26% to -46% across subtasks compared to LAB-Bench; no single specific best-model percentage is given in the abstract.
search_tools_named: web search and code execution as the primary augmentation tools compared against base (tool-free) models; DbQA2 additionally requires navigating specialized scientific/database APIs (with nontrivial schema/identifiers), and SeqQA2/CloningQA context can be delivered via file upload instead of inline prompting
task_summary: Given a biology research question, search literature, databases, or sequence files to extract precise facts, figures, or perform lab-protocol reasoning.
task_phrase: data access is assessed with DbQA, a set of tasks requiring access to specific entries in (sometimes multiple) biological databases to answer accurately

title: LEAP: Likelihood Elicitation and Aggregation for LLM-based Probabilistic Forecasting
search_tools_named: web search call and page fetch call sharing a single backend (own agent loop); also evaluated on several agent CLI frameworks

task_phrase: we construct a benchmark covering forecasting, information-seeking, and browsing tasks on which LEAP improves prediction accuracy and probabilistic quality across multiple base models and several agent CLI frameworks

title: LFRAG: Layout-oriented Fine-grained Retrieval-Augmented Generation on Multimodal Document Understanding
headline_result: LFRAG achieves state-of-the-art retrieval performance on LFDocQA, outperforms the best baseline by 7.20% in answer accuracy, and reduces token consumption by 73.07% in generation tasks.

title: Reproducing Complex Set-Compositional Information Retrieval

availability: code and LIMIT+ data generation scripts are released (no specific single URL given in the abstract).

title: LakeQA: An Exploratory QA Benchmark over a Million-Scale Data Lake
headline_result: GPT-5.2 achieves only an exact-match score of 18.37% on LakeQA among seven evaluated frontier LLMs; abstract does not state a human performance figure for comparison.

task_summary: Given a question whose evidence is hidden in a huge document collection, iteratively search, download, and inspect files to find the answer.

title: Learning to Remember: End-to-End Training of Memory Agents for Long-Context Reasoning

title: LegalCiteTrust: Benchmarking Citation Trustworthiness in Chinese Long-Form Legal Research Reports

title: LiveBrowseComp: Are Search Agents Searching, or Just Verifying What They Already Know?

## Abstract

 Large Language Models (LLMs), despite their advancements, are fundamentally limited by their static parametric knowledge, hindering performance on tasks requiring open-domain up-to-date information.
While enabling LLMs to interact with external knowledge environments is a promising solution, current efforts primarily address closed-end problems. Open-ended questions, which characterized by lacking a standard answer or providing non-unique and diverse answers, remain underexplored.
To bridge this gap, we present O 2 -Searcher, a novel search agent leveraging reinforcement learning to effectively tackle both open-ended and closed-ended questions in the open domain. O 2 -Searcher leverages an efficient, locally simulated search environment for dynamic knowledge acquisition, effectively decoupling the external world knowledge from model’s sophisticated reasoning processes.
